construct: With the first breaths, pulmonary vascular resistance falls and pulmonary blood flow rises. Increased pulmonary venous return raises left atrial pressure. Simultaneously, loss of placental venous return reduces right-sided filling. The resulting left-to-right atrial pressure reversal presses the septum primum against the septum secundum, functionally closing the foramen ovale.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Normal neonatal transition lowers pulmonary vascular resistance, increases pulmonary venous return, raises left atrial pressure, and pushes septum primum against septum secundum.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: A rise in right atrial pressure is physiologically plausible in fetal circulation but would maintain rather than close the right-to-left atrial shunt.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Only left-atrial pressure exceeding right-atrial pressure directly provides the mechanical force for functional foramen-ovale closure.
